Folks —

I reviewed Redwood_MSA_redlines_20270620.pdf and highlighted three seats of negotiation that will affect Sterling's procurement acceptance:

1) Indemnity cap: Sterling proposes unlimited indemnity for third-party claims arising from data processing. We can accept a mutual indemnity with a damages cap tied to the Order Form value (standard for our enterprise offers). Suggested language provided in the PDF comments.

2) Data residency: Sterling wants explicit language guaranteeing EU data storage for EU-subject records. Our stance: contractually commit to processing region for customer-controlled data only and offer a path to put a contract addendum for full regional hosting guarantees. For procurement this can be reflected as a staged SOW/addendum.

3) PO field requirements: Procurement flagged that Ariba validation rejects when the remit address doesn't match the vendor profile. Rafael — on the Order Form we must include a "Remit-To Address" field and a structured "Tax ID" field. Confirm with Sterling whether the remit-to will be a US address or an alternate remit (they might prefer a payment agent).

Action items:
- Rafael: ask Sterling to confirm GL code + remit-to address (single line).
- Marissa: if Sterling insists on full data residency in the MSA we will need Product + Infra input; please flag risk to go/no-go.
- I'll prepare a clean MSA and an addendum template by Mon 2027-06-28 to circulate for signature.

Laura Bennett
Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Phone: 650-555-2241
